tier_key: A = approved drug / strong human RCTs · B = multiple human trials, mixed or non-US · C = limited human / Russian or small trials · D = preclinical / single-lineage / no combination data.
disclaimer: Research use only. Not for human or animal consumption. Not medical advice.

cards.name: GLOW
cards.identity: Market nickname for a three-peptide research blend, not a single molecule. Common label: GHK-Cu ~50 mg + BPC-157 ~10 mg + TB-500 ~10 mg (≈70 mg). Ratios vary by vendor; the name is not a pharmacopeial standard.
cards.tier: D for the blend. Component tiers differ (GHK-Cu topical human cosmetic data; BPC-157 mostly animal; TB-500 fragment thin; parent thymosin β4 has some wound/ophthalmic trials).
cards.what_exists: Separate literatures for each peptide. No published controlled study of GHK-Cu + BPC-157 + TB-500 together in any species.
cards.regulatory: Not FDA-approved. BPC-157 and related peptides have been in FDA compounding / Category 2 discussions; PCAC votes are non-binding until rulemaking.
cards.caveats: Synergy is inferred. Copper from GHK-Cu could affect other peptides; not studied. Injectable GHK-Cu is not the same evidence base as topical cosmetic GHK-Cu. Confirm each component on the lot COA.
cards.sources: Pickart & Margolina, Int J Mol Sci 2018 (PMID 29986520); HSS Journal 2025 BPC-157 systematic review; thymosin β4 Phase 2 wound / RGN-259 ophthalmic work (parent protein, not the fragment); FDA PCAC / NYT / Science coverage of 2026 compounding votes.
cards.catalog_keys: `GLOW Blend (GHK-Cu/BPC-157/TB-500) | Vial | 50-70mg` (Royal Peptides). Related: Wolverine (BPC-157/TB-500), KLOW, GHK-Cu, BPC-157, TB-500, KPV as singles.

cards.name: KLOW
cards.identity: GLOW plus KPV. Common label: GHK-Cu ~50 mg + BPC-157 ~10 mg + TB-500 ~10 mg + KPV ~10 mg (≈80 mg).
cards.tier: D for the blend.
cards.what_exists: Same three literatures as GLOW, plus KPV mouse colitis / NF-κB work. Zero peer-reviewed studies of the four-peptide combination. Closest published combo is a small uncontrolled knee series of BPC-157 ± thymosin β4 — not KLOW.
cards.regulatory: Not approved. Same compounding caveats as the components.
cards.caveats: Fixed 5:1:1:1 ratio may not match doses used in any single-agent study. Half-lives differ (BPC-157 short in animals; tripeptides clear fast). WADA lists thymosin β4 / TB-500 (S2).
cards.sources: Dalmasso et al., Gastroenterology 2008 (PMID 18061177) — PepT1-mediated KPV uptake, DSS/TNBS colitis in mice; Kelly / Getting α-MSH fragment NF-κB papers; same GHK-Cu / BPC-157 / Tβ4 sources as GLOW.
cards.catalog_keys: `KLOW (BPC-157/TB-500/GHK-Cu/KPV) | Vial | 80mg` (Royal Peptides). Related: GLOW, Wolverine, KPV, GHK-Cu / KPV nasal combos on some vendors.

cards.name: KPV
cards.identity: Lys-Pro-Val, C-terminal tripeptide of α-MSH.
cards.tier: D (preclinical). Strong mechanism papers; no human efficacy trials in the file.
cards.what_exists: Inhibits NF-κB / MAPK; taken up via PepT1 in gut epithelium and immune cells; reduced colitis markers in DSS and TNBS mice.
cards.regulatory: Not approved. Appeared in 2026 PCAC compounding discussion with other research peptides.
cards.sources: PMID 18061177; related α-MSH fragment papers (PMID 16274845 and reviews).
cards.formats: vial, nasal, oral on some vendors.

cards.name: BPC-157
cards.identity: Synthetic 15-aa gastric pentadecapeptide.
cards.tier: D for human use; large preclinical file, almost all from one research lineage plus limited independent mechanism work.
cards.what_exists: Rodent tendon, muscle, gut, vascular models. 2025 HSS Journal review: nearly all preclinical; one small retrospective human series. FDA staff have argued chemical characterization and human safety data are insufficient; 2026 PCAC voted to recommend 503A listing (non-binding).
cards.caveats: Not FDA-approved. Gray-market quality issues documented in general peptide testing literature. No adequate RCTs.
cards.sources: HSS Journal 2025 systematic review; FDA PCAC briefing / NYT 23 Jul 2026; Science / MedPage Today on the same meeting.
cards.formats: vial, nasal, oral, blends (Wolverine, GLOW, KLOW).

cards.name: TB-500
cards.identity: Synthetic fragment (often Ac-LKKTETQ) of thymosin β4 — not the full 43-aa protein.
cards.tier: D for the fragment. Parent Tβ4 has more human wound / ophthalmic data.
cards.what_exists: Animal migration / angiogenesis models. Phase 2 topical Tβ4 wound data and RGN-259 ophthalmic trials apply to the parent protein.
cards.caveats: Do not treat Tβ4 trial results as TB-500 results. WADA S2. PCAC discussed injectable TB-500 in 2026.
cards.sources: Tβ4 wound / Sosne ophthalmic literature; FDA staff notes on scarce human data for the fragment.

cards.name: GHK-Cu
cards.identity: Gly-His-Lys copper(II) complex; endogenous tripeptide.
cards.tier: B–C topical cosmetic; D for injectable / systemic claims.
cards.what_exists: Extensive in-vitro gene-expression work (~thousands of genes). Small IRB cosmetic trials of topical GHK-Cu (wrinkle / collagen histology). Plasma levels decline with age in observational work.
cards.caveats: Topical ≠ injectable. Copper load and peptide stability in multi-peptide vials are not characterized in the file.
cards.sources: PMID 29986520; Pickart historical isolation work; topical cosmetic trials cited in evidence reviews.
cards.formats: vial, nasal, oral on some vendors; dominant mass in GLOW/KLOW.

cards.name: Selank
cards.identity: Heptapeptide tuftsin analog (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro).
cards.tier: C. Russian anxiolytic registration; limited English-language RCTs.
cards.what_exists: GAD clinical reports; GABA allosteric / gene-expression work; rodent memory models.

cards.name: Semax
cards.identity: ACTH(4-10) analog Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro.
cards.tier: C. Russian approval for stroke / cognition; BDNF work in animals; limited human.

cards.name: Epitalon (Epithalon)
cards.identity: Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly pineal tetrapeptide.
cards.tier: D. Cell/rodent telomerase and lifespan work mostly from one Russian group; 2025 Brunel in-vitro confirmation of hTERT upregulation also noted ALT in cancer lines.
cards.sources: PMID 40908429; Int J Mol Sci 2025 overview PMID 40141333.
cards.formats: vial, nasal, oral on some vendors.

cards.name: Thymosin Alpha-1 (thymalfasin)
cards.identity: 28-aa thymic peptide.
cards.tier: B. Many human trials (hepatitis, immune adjunct, mixed sepsis/COVID). Approved in numerous countries; not broadly FDA-approved. US compounding restricted for most uses since ~2023. Large 2025 sepsis trial (TESTS) negative on 28-day mortality.
cards.sources: PMID 38308608; TESTS trial coverage; hepatitis meta-analyses.
cards.formats: vial, nasal, oral on some vendors.

cards.name: SS-31 (elamipretide)
cards.identity: Mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide (Szeto-Schiller 31).
cards.tier: B for Barth syndrome (FDA accelerated approval 2025, FORZINITY); mixed/failed for primary mitochondrial myopathy and several heart trials. Strong aged-mouse muscle energetics data.
cards.caveats: Do not generalize Barth approval to research-chemical vials sold for other uses.
cards.formats: vial, nasal, oral on some vendors.

cards.name: Melanotan 2
cards.identity: Non-selective melanocortin agonist.
cards.tier: C for pigmentation / erectile signals in tiny early Arizona trials; safety file is case reports (priapism, hypertension, naevi change, melanoma signal unresolved). Not approved anywhere. PT-141 is the related approved sexual-dysfunction drug (different product).
cards.sources: Dorr / Wessells early trials; Clinical Toxicology case-series reviews.

cards.name: LL-37
cards.identity: Human cathelicidin fragment.
cards.tier: C. Broad antimicrobial mechanism; HEAL LL-37 Phase 2b venous-ulcer RCT missed primary endpoint; subgroup signal in large ulcers.

cards.name: VIP (aviptadil)
cards.identity: 28-aa neuropeptide.
cards.tier: C. Small PAH open study; COVID respiratory-failure RCT missed primary endpoint. Extremely short plasma half-life.

cards.name: hCG
cards.identity: Glycoprotein hormone. FDA-approved since 1967 for ovulation trigger and labeled male hypogonadism / cryptorchidism uses.
cards.tier: A for labeled fertility uses. Not approved for weight loss.
cards.formats: IU vials on some vendors. Research-chemical lots are not the licensed drug.

cards.name: Mazdutide
cards.identity: GLP-1 / glucagon dual agonist (Innovent). Phase 3 weight and T2D data in Chinese adults; NMPA approval in China reported; not FDA-approved.
cards.tier: B (strong RCTs, limited geography).

cards.name: SLU-PP-332
cards.identity: Small-molecule ERR pan-agonist, not a peptide.
cards.tier: D. Mouse endurance / metabolic papers only. No human trials in the file.

cards.name: HGH fragment 176-191
cards.identity: C-terminal GH fragment. Preclinical lipolysis from one group; stabilized analog AOD-9604 failed large human weight-loss trials.
cards.tier: D.

cards.name: Cardiogen
cards.identity: AEDR tetrapeptide, Khavinson cardiac bioregulator.
cards.tier: D. Organotypic / rodent work from one lineage. No human trials in the file.

cards.name: Thymalin
cards.identity: Bovine thymic peptide mixture (not the same as thymosin α1).
cards.tier: D–C. Long Russian observational elderly cohorts; no Western RCTs.

cards.name: AHK-Cu
cards.identity: Ala-His-Lys-copper. One 2007 ex-vivo human follicle paper (PMID 17703734). No in-vivo human trials. Do not recycle GHK-Cu claims.

cards.name: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin)
cards.identity: Ghrelin-receptor GH secretagogue. Japanese diagnostic GH-stimulation data; not FDA-approved.
cards.tier: C for diagnostic use in that program.

cards.name: ACE-031
cards.identity: Soluble ActRIIB-Fc myostatin-pathway blocker.
cards.tier: C early human (lean mass after single dose); DMD trial stopped for vascular AEs (epistaxis, telangiectasia). Development halted.

cards.name: AICAR
cards.identity: AMPK-activating nucleoside, not a peptide. Mouse “exercise mimetic” data; WADA-prohibited. Limited human.

cards.name: Oxytocin
cards.identity: Nonapeptide. FDA-approved for labor induction and postpartum hemorrhage.
cards.tier: A for labeled obstetric uses. Intranasal / obesity RCTs mixed (one 8-week obesity RCT no weight change). Research vials are not the licensed drug product.

cards.name: Melatonin
cards.identity: Pineal hormone; US dietary supplement, not an FDA-approved drug (agonists ramelteon / tasimelteon are).
cards.tier: B for jet lag and modest sleep-onset latency in meta-analyses.
cards.formats: some vendors list melatonin packs; quality varies in the supplement market.

cards.name: Other catalog notes
cards.notes: - Semaglutide / tirzepatide / retatrutide: approved or late-stage incretins when they are the licensed product. Research-chemical vials are not those products. Do not imply interchangeability. - Wolverine blend: BPC-157 + TB-500 only. Same “no combination trial” rule. - Semax + Selank combos: two Russian nootropics in one vial; no combination RCT in the file.

cards.name: Quality / testing
cards.identity: COA and vendor-testing literacy for this site.
cards.what_exists: A COA can show HPLC purity, MS identity, sometimes content, sometimes endotoxin / metals / sterility. A COA cannot show that the material is safe or effective in people. Ask for the COA that matches the lot number, with a named laboratory and a date. Vendor testing claims on this site are taken from each vendor’s own published material and grouped by how far an outsider could check them.
cards.caveats: A COA cannot show that the material is safe or effective in people.
